messages:
maria: Heads-up: we've been getting inconsistent semantics from SDKs around absent vs empty attributes (billing_key, tenant_id). Want to decide an ingestion contract so downstream billing and joins are deterministic.
kevin: I'm leaning toward treating missing = unknown and reserving empty-string as explicit user-set. Smaller payloads if SDKs omit optional keys. But billing routers need a definite key.
sara: Problem: some analytic joins assume attribute exists and index on it. If we drop keys we'll increase cardinality of 'unknown' and break dashboards.
maria: Options: 1) Require billing_key always present (SDKs enforced) 2) Allow missing but enrich at ingest to infer a billing_key, tagging it as inferred 3) Keep optional but add per-field presence flags in envelope. Thoughts?
tomas: (3) adds complexity across many SDKs and is annoying for ad-hoc telemetry consumers. (1) is safest but slows SDK rollout. (2) seems like a middle ground if enrichment is auditable and reversible.
kevin: Auditable is key. If we infer one billing_key incorrectly, it can mess billing. We need provenance: mark inferred vs raw, and probably keep original raw envelope for a short window.
sara: Implementation idea: enrichment pipeline add two fields: attrs_provenance (map of key->"raw|inferred|normalized") and envelope.schema_version. Ingest will set billing_key inferred when missing and set attrs_provenance[billing_key] = "inferred".
maria: That aligns with legal/compliance needs. We should also publish SDK guidance: prefer omission for optional attrs; if you send empty string it's considered present.
tomas: Practically, map<string,string> provenance bloats payloads. Alternative: provenance is an array of well-known keys with bit flags, and a compact bitmask for others. Keep it opt-in via envelope flags.
kevin: Also add metrics: ingest.enrichment.attempts, ingest.enrichment.success, ingest.enrichment.confidence_bucket. We'll need a dashboard to monitor inferred vs explicit billing volume.
sara: Migration plan: stage 1) add schema_version to envelopes and support old behavior; stage 2) start enriching missing billing_key but keep original; stage 3) after monitoring window, update RFC to change expectation. We'll need at least one SDK release where we still send billing_key to avoid a gap.
maria: Timeline proposal: RFC + proto diff this week, ingest adapter PoC next week, 2-week canary where enrichment is enabled for small tenants only, full rollout after metrics look stable.
tomas: Edge cases: multi-tenant aliases, header canonicalization, and service-account flows where tenant header absent. Enrichment should be deterministic: prefer tenant header, else token metadata lookup. Cache results to avoid extra backend load.
kevin: For determinism, record the resolver version used in attrs_provenance or envelope.meta so we can replay. Also include a checksum of the original envelope when we store the raw for 7 days.
sara: For storage, instead of full raw store for everyone, only keep raw diffs for cases where enrichment changes billing attribution. That limits cost.
maria: Action items: maria -> draft RFC + proto patch (include schema_version int and optional provenance structure); kevin -> cost estimate for provenance payload and raw-diff storage; sara -> write enrichment heuristics and a minimal test harness; tomas -> prototype idempotent enrichment adapter and caching.
ingest-bot: deploy: created feature-flag ingest.enrichment.infer_billing_key (default off).
kevin: I'll add a couple of counters and a dashboard. Can we also gate enrichment behind a tenant-opt-in tag so early adopters can help validate?
sara: Yes. We'll expose an opt-in tenant flag in the tenant config service.
maria: OK - I'll post RFC link in #eng-platform when ready and schedule a 30m demo next Wed. Thanks! :thumbsup:
